about: The library transition table of the heap core (references, layer 2): one row per built-in operation lean reads through the heap. Each row states what ECMA-262 (edition 2027, section ids as on tc39.es/ecma262) or the HTML standard fixes about the operation, at the level the proof needs: does it allocate, does it change its receiver, what identity it returns, in what order it visits, what a callback may do, and when it throws. heap.mjs generates one total Dafny function per row and per shape from the `dafny` template (`<K>` the shape key, `<E>` the element Dafny type); design/library-ops.dfy holds the monomorphic forms verified with dafny 4.11.0 (23 verified, 0 errors). A row whose `status` is `draft` is not generated. Lane B's call recorder (exec/transitions.mjs) checks every observed call against its row; a mismatch refuses the row's proofs until the row is fixed. Version 2 (2026-10-27): the Map cell is (keys, m), an insertion-ordered key list beside a Dafny map, so repeated writes are idempotent by the map's laws. A row whose `lane` is `ordinary` (stage 5, design/library-rows.md) is read by the ordinary translator (translate.mjs) in the value model (a sequence, a string, a number): its `dafny` field is that reading, `reading` says whether it is exact, uninterpreted (a bodiless function of the value, the same on both sides) or a world read (a bodiless transition), and heap.mjs instantiates none of them. An `ordinary` field on a heap row is the value-model reading of the same operation used as a value.

operations.resultMeaning: the new length
operations.throws: Set with throw; TypeError past 2^53-1 (not modelled: the sequence is unbounded)
operations.dafny: function Push_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, v: <E>): HWorld { if Is<K>(hw, r) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(hw.heap[r].items + [v])]) else hw }

operations.resultMeaning: the new length
operations.order: arguments in order, placed before the existing items
operations.dafny: function Unshift_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, v: <E>): HWorld { if Is<K>(hw, r) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>([v] + hw.heap[r].items)]) else hw }

operations.resultMeaning: the removed last element, undefined on an empty array
operations.dafny: function Pop_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref): HWorld { if Is<K>(hw, r) && |hw.heap[r].items| > 0 then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(hw.heap[r].items[..|hw.heap[r].items| - 1])]) else hw }

ordinary.use: a value: on a fresh array, or on a local array the function owns where the call runs on every path of its statement and the statement reads the array nowhere else
ordinary.dafny: At_<E>(xs, -1) as the value (None on an empty array); the local is rebound to (if |xs| > 0 then xs[..|xs| - 1] else xs) before the statement

operations.resultMeaning: the removed first element, undefined on an empty array
operations.order: first item, the rest shifted down
operations.dafny: function Shift_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref): HWorld { if Is<K>(hw, r) && |hw.heap[r].items| > 0 then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(hw.heap[r].items[1..])]) else hw }

ordinary.dafny: At_<E>(xs, 0) as the value (None on an empty array); the local is rebound to (if |xs| > 0 then xs[1..] else xs) before the statement

operations.resultMeaning: a fresh array of the removed elements (ArraySpeciesCreate)
operations.order: indices in order; start and delete count clamped as the spec's ToIntegerOrInfinity steps
operations.callback: none (a species constructor can run code: refused by the lint when the receiver is a subclass)
operations.throws: species and property operations with throw
operations.dafny: function Splice_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, start: int, dc: int, ins: seq<<E>>): (HWorld, Ref) { var xs := Items_<K>(hw, r); var s := Clamp(start, 0, |xs|); var d := Clamp(dc, 0, |xs| - s); var removed := xs[s .. s + d]; var h1 := if Is<K>(hw, r) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(xs[..s] + ins + xs[s + d ..])]) else hw; if Is<K>(hw, r) then Alloc_<K>(h1, removed) else (hw, hw.next) }

ordinary.use: as pop; also the statement form, whose start now counts from the end when negative (23.1.3.31 step 6)
ordinary.dafny: var s := SeqClamp(if start < 0 then |xs| + start else start, 0, |xs|); var d := (no start: 0; no count: |xs| - s; else SeqClamp(count, 0, |xs| - s)); the value xs[s..s + d], the local rebound to xs[..s] + items + xs[s + d..]

operations.resultMeaning: the receiver itself
operations.order: pairwise Get, Set, Delete from both ends
operations.dafny: function Reverse_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref): (HWorld, Ref) { (if Is<K>(hw, r) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(Rev_<K>(hw.heap[r].items))]) else hw, r) }

operations.resultMeaning: the receiver itself
operations.order: an implementation-defined sequence of comparator calls; stable for a consistent comparator
operations.callback: pure-required (a comparator with effects or an inconsistent one has no portable meaning: obligation `comparator effect`, ASK)
operations.throws: TypeError when the comparator is neither undefined nor callable; an abrupt comparator stops further calls
operations.dafny:
function StableSortBy_<K>(xs: seq<<E>>, lt: (<E>, <E>) -> bool): seq<<E>>
function SortPure_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, lt: (<E>, <E>) -> bool): (HWorld, Ref) { (if Is<K>(hw, r) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(StableSortBy_<K>(hw.heap[r].items, lt))]) else hw, r) }
operations.note: StableSortBy_ is a bodiless function: an uninterpreted stable sort by the comparator's order, the same on both sides (the theorem refuses {:extern}, {:axiom} and assume anywhere a proof can see). Two sorts are equal when their items and comparators are; a changed comparator is unproved and left to lane B.

operations.resultMeaning: a fresh array (ArraySpeciesCreate); object elements stay shared
operations.throws: species and getters observable: refused by the lint on a subclass or an accessor element
operations.dafny: function Slice_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, s: int, e: int): (HWorld, Ref) { var xs := Items_<K>(hw, r); var a := Clamp(s, 0, |xs|); var b := Clamp(e, a, |xs|); Alloc_<K>(hw, xs[a .. b]) }

operations.resultMeaning: a fresh array: the receiver's items then each argument's
operations.order: receiver, then arguments in order; IsConcatSpreadable reads a Symbol-keyed property (refused on a subclass)
operations.dafny: function Concat_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, q: Ref): (HWorld, Ref) { Alloc_<K>(hw, Items_<K>(hw, r) + Items_<K>(hw, q)) }

operations.resultMeaning: a fresh array of the callback's results
operations.order: present indices ascending over the range fixed before the first call; holes skipped and kept
operations.callback: pure-required (an effectful callback is the loop reading of translate.mjs, not this row)
operations.dafny: function Map_<K>_<K2>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, f: <E> -> <E2>): (HWorld, Ref) { var xs := Items_<K>(hw, r); Alloc_<K2>(hw, seq(|xs|, i requires 0 <= i < |xs| => f(xs[i]))) }

operations.resultMeaning: a fresh array of the kept elements; object elements stay shared
operations.order: present indices ascending over the range fixed before the first call
operations.dafny: function Filter_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, p: <E> -> bool): (HWorld, Ref) { Alloc_<K>(hw, Keep_<K>(Items_<K>(hw, r), p)) }

operations.resultMeaning: the same Map
operations.order: insertion order; an existing key keeps its position
operations.throws: TypeError on a non-Map receiver (the type excludes it)
operations.keyRule: CanonicalizeKeyedCollectionKey (24.5.1: -0 becomes +0) then SameValue; object keys by identity
operations.dafny: function MapSet_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, k: <KT>, v: <E>): (HWorld, Ref) { (if Is<K>(hw, r) && !(k in hw.heap[r].m && hw.heap[r].m[k] == v) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(if k in hw.heap[r].m then hw.heap[r].keys else hw.heap[r].keys + [k], hw.heap[r].m[k := v])]) else hw, r) }
operations.note: A Map cell is its insertion-ordered key list and a Dafny map (version 2 of the cell, 2026-10-27): a repeated set of one key to one value is the same cell by the map update laws, so idempotent writes prove without a lemma; the entry list of version 1 needed an induction the theorem never writes. A write that changes nothing (a key already holding the value, a member already present, an absent key or member deleted) returns the world itself, so a repeated write is the same term and proves equal without map or sequence extensionality (2026-10-27).

operations.resultMeaning: the value under the key, undefined when absent
operations.dafny: function MapGet_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, k: <KT>): Option<<E>> { if Is<K>(hw, r) && k in hw.heap[r].m then Some(hw.heap[r].m[k]) else None }
operations.note: A Map cell is its insertion-ordered key list and a Dafny map (version 2 of the cell, 2026-10-27): a repeated set of one key to one value is the same cell by the map update laws, so idempotent writes prove without a lemma; the entry list of version 1 needed an induction the theorem never writes.

operations.resultMeaning: a boolean
operations.dafny: function MapHas_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, k: <KT>): bool { Is<K>(hw, r) && k in hw.heap[r].m }
operations.note: A Map cell is its insertion-ordered key list and a Dafny map (version 2 of the cell, 2026-10-27): a repeated set of one key to one value is the same cell by the map update laws, so idempotent writes prove without a lemma; the entry list of version 1 needed an induction the theorem never writes.

operations.resultMeaning: true when a key was removed
operations.order: the remaining entries keep their order
operations.dafny: function MapDelete_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, k: <KT>): HWorld { if Is<K>(hw, r) && k in hw.heap[r].m then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(RemoveKey_<K>(hw.heap[r].keys, k), hw.heap[r].m - {k})]) else hw }
operations.note: A Map cell is its insertion-ordered key list and a Dafny map (version 2 of the cell, 2026-10-27): a repeated set of one key to one value is the same cell by the map update laws, so idempotent writes prove without a lemma; the entry list of version 1 needed an induction the theorem never writes. A write that changes nothing (a key already holding the value, a member already present, an absent key or member deleted) returns the world itself, so a repeated write is the same term and proves equal without map or sequence extensionality (2026-10-27).

operations.resultMeaning: the same Set
operations.order: insertion order; a present value is a no-op
operations.throws: TypeError on a non-Set receiver (the type excludes it)
operations.dafny: function SetAdd_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, v: <E>): (HWorld, Ref) { (if Is<K>(hw, r) && v !in hw.heap[r].items then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(hw.heap[r].items + [v])]) else hw, r) }
operations.note: A write that changes nothing (a key already holding the value, a member already present, an absent key or member deleted) returns the world itself, so a repeated write is the same term and proves equal without map or sequence extensionality (2026-10-27).

operations.resultMeaning: a boolean
operations.dafny: function SetHas_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, v: <E>): bool { Is<K>(hw, r) && v in hw.heap[r].items }

operations.resultMeaning: true when the value was present
operations.order: the remaining items keep their order
operations.dafny: function SetDelete_<K>(hw: HWorld, r: Ref, v: <E>): HWorld { if Is<K>(hw, r) && v in hw.heap[r].items then hw.(heap := hw.heap[r := <K>(RemoveItem_<K>(hw.heap[r].items, v))]) else hw }
operations.note: A write that changes nothing (a key already holding the value, a member already present, an absent key or member deleted) returns the world itself, so a repeated write is the same term and proves equal without map or sequence extensionality (2026-10-27).

operations.resultMeaning: the target itself
operations.order: sources in order; each source's own enumerable keys in [[OwnPropertyKeys]] order; Get then Set with throw
operations.callback: none (a getter on a source or a setter on the target runs code: refused by the lint, obligation `accessor`)
operations.throws: a Set with throw after earlier writes: partial writes survive (not modelled: the lint refuses frozen or accessor targets)
operations.dafny: function Assign_<K>(hw: HWorld, t: Ref, s: Ref): (HWorld, Ref) { (if Is<K>(hw, t) && Is<K>(hw, s) then hw.(heap := hw.heap[t := hw.heap[s]]) else hw, t) }
operations.note: the generated form copies every field when source and target share a shape; a source of another shape copies the fields it has, field by field through Set_

operations.resultMeaning: the object itself
operations.dafny: // refused by the lint (rule `freeze`): in strict code a write to a frozen object throws, and the value reading has no fault channel for that write; a frozen set in HWorld with silent no-op writes would prove a throwing candidate equal to one that writes nothing
operations.note: Decided 2026-10-27: refused by name until the heap core carries a fault channel; seal and preventExtensions alike.

operations.resultMeaning: a fresh graph; sharing and cycles inside the input are preserved in the copy; a class instance becomes a plain object
operations.order: a memory map keyed by the input's objects
operations.throws: DataCloneError on a Symbol, a function, a DOM node; transfer detaches the source
operations.dafny: // Clone_<K> is Alloc_<K> of the source cell's own contents: a record of primitives, an array, Set or Map of primitives, or a Date; one level, a nested graph is refused by the lint (`clone of a nested graph`); the value reading takes the copy as the value itself
operations.note: Built 2026-10-27 in the heap core and the ordinary lane; cycles and nested references wait for the canonical-heap certificate.

operations.resultMeaning: a setter returns the new time value, a number, never the Date
operations.throws: none; an invalid Date is NaN; setFullYear on a NaN time value starts from +0 (21.4.4.21), the other setters give NaN
operations.dafny: datatype D = D(tv: NUM); Alloc_D(hw, tv) for new Date(n); Get_D_tv for getTime and valueOf; function DateUTC_<getter>(tv: NUM): NUM bodiless for the UTC getters; a setter and a local-time getter are world transitions of the ordinary lane (the Date's state lives in the world), outside the core
operations.note: Built 2026-10-27: new Date(n) with one time value, getTime, valueOf and the UTC getters in the heap core; the setters and the local-time getters read or write the host's time zone, so they stay world transitions of the ordinary lane, ordered with every other Date method on the same handle; new Date() with no argument is the clock read; a string argument is parsing, refused.

operations.resultMeaning: the receiver itself, every index in [start, end) set to the value
operations.throws: Set with throw (not reached on an ordinary array)
operations.dafny: (var xs := R; var lo := SeqClamp(rel(start, 0)); var hi := SeqClamp(rel(end, |xs|)); seq(|xs|, (i: int) requires 0 <= i < |xs| => if lo <= i < hi then v else xs[i])), rel counting a negative bound from the end
operations.note: Admitted on a fresh receiver only (new Array(n), Array(n), Array.from, a literal, a copy): the result is the receiver, so on a name it would be a second name for a changed array.

operations.resultMeaning: a new array, the receiver's elements sorted (SortIndexedProperties with the comparator, or the default string order)
operations.callback: a pure comparator (the lint refuses an effect in it)
operations.dafny: function sort_<E>(xs: seq<<E>>, cmp: (<E>, <E>) -> NUM): seq<<E>> and function sort_default_<E>(xs: seq<<E>>): seq<<E>>, bodiless: the same functions as [...xs].sort(cmp) and [...xs].sort()

operations.resultMeaning: a new array, the receiver's elements in reverse order
operations.dafny: Reverse_<E>(xs)

operations.resultMeaning: the last element the predicate accepts, undefined when none
operations.callback: a pure predicate of the element (an index parameter is refused: it counts from the end)
operations.dafny: Find_<E>(Reverse_<E>(xs), p): the first match of the reversed sequence

operations.resultMeaning: the index of the last element the predicate accepts, -1 when none
operations.callback: a pure predicate of the element
operations.dafny: (var k := FindIndex_<E>(Reverse_<E>(xs), p); if k < 0 then -1 else |xs| - 1 - k)

operations.resultMeaning: the last index holding a value strictly equal to the argument, -1 when none
operations.dafny: (var k := IndexOf_<E>(Reverse_<E>(xs), x); if k < 0 then -1 else |xs| - 1 - k)
operations.note: Primitive elements only: strict equality on objects is identity, which the value model does not hold; a fromIndex argument stays out.

operations.resultMeaning: this.join(): the elements' ToString joined by commas, null and undefined as empty
operations.dafny: Join_string(xs, ",") on strings; on other elements the same uninterpreted array_join as xs.join()

operations.resultMeaning: Number::toString(x, 10) with no radix: ToString(x)
operations.throws: RangeError on a radix outside 2 to 36 (a radix stays on the earlier uninterpreted method reading)
operations.dafny: function to_string(x: NUM): string, bodiless: the function a template literal reads for ${x}

operations.resultMeaning: BigInt::toString(x, 10) with no radix: ToString(x)
operations.throws: RangeError on a radix outside 2 to 36 (a radix stays out)
operations.dafny: function to_string(x: int): string, bodiless, the template literal's function

operations.resultMeaning: "true" or "false"
operations.dafny: (if b then "true" else "false")

operations.resultMeaning: the string itself
operations.dafny: s
operations.note: A union of string, number, bigint and boolean reads x.toString() as ToString(x), the template literal's to_string of the union's datatype; a union with an object member stays out (an object's toString is its own method).

operations.resultMeaning: the number formatted by the host's locale data and the given locales and options
operations.throws: RangeError on an invalid locale or option (inside the transition)
operations.dafny: function <NUM>_toLocaleString(w: World, x: NUM, args...): (World, string), bodiless: a transition, ordered with every other effect
operations.note: BigInt.prototype.toLocaleString (21.2.3.2) is the transition bigint_toLocaleString, a distinct function. Outside callbacks only.

operations.resultMeaning: the string lower-cased by the host's or the given locale's case mappings
operations.dafny: function str_toLocaleLowerCase(w: World, s: string, args...): (World, string), bodiless

operations.resultMeaning: the run of at most length code units from start, a negative start counted from the end
operations.dafny: StrSubstr_string(s, a, len): lo := a < 0 ? max(|s| + a, 0) : min(a, |s|); l := clamp(len, 0, |s|); s[lo..min(lo + l, |s|)]

operations.resultMeaning: the index of the first match, -1 when none; lastIndex is saved, set to 0 and restored
operations.dafny: function str_search(s: string, pattern): int, bodiless: a function of the string and the pattern's source and flags (RegExp.prototype[@@search] restores lastIndex)

operations.resultMeaning: a new RegExpStringIterator over the global matches, starting at the pattern's lastIndex
operations.throws: TypeError when a RegExp pattern lacks the g flag
operations.dafny: function str_matchAll(s: string, pattern): Ext_RegExpStringIterator, bodiless; a for-of over it reads Ext_RegExpStringIterator_to_seq, bodiless
operations.note: Admitted with a regular expression literal carrying g (a new object, lastIndex 0) or a string pattern (RegExpCreate(s, "g")); a named RegExp may carry a moved lastIndex and stays out. A spread of the iterator stays refused by the spread rule.

helpers.Clamp: function Clamp(i: int, lo: int, hi: int): int { if i < lo then lo else if i > hi then hi else i }
helpers.Rev_<K>: function Rev_<K>(xs: seq<<E>>): seq<<E>> decreases |xs| { if |xs| == 0 then [] else Rev_<K>(xs[1..]) + [xs[0]] }
helpers.Keep_<K>: function Keep_<K>(xs: seq<<E>>, p: <E> -> bool): seq<<E>> decreases |xs| { if |xs| == 0 then [] else (if p(xs[0]) then [xs[0]] else []) + Keep_<K>(xs[1..], p) }
helpers.RemoveKey_<K>: function RemoveKey_<K>(ks: seq<<KT>>, k: <KT>): seq<<KT>> decreases |ks| { if |ks| == 0 then [] else (if ks[0] == k then [] else [ks[0]]) + RemoveKey_<K>(ks[1..], k) }
helpers.RemoveItem_<K>: function RemoveItem_<K>(xs: seq<<E>>, v: <E>): seq<<E>> decreases |xs| { if |xs| == 0 then [] else (if xs[0] == v then [] else [xs[0]]) + RemoveItem_<K>(xs[1..], v) }
